questions.question: When parking by backing up and to the left, a driver should:

options.text: Move forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then move forward to the left.
Move forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: To park by backing up and to the left, first move forward straight, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space lines.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction they are turning.
Look in the opposite direction.
Look behind their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction they are turning.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers usually look in the direction of the turn. Even without a turn signal, a driver's body position can show that they plan to turn.

questions.question: A standee line on a bus shows:

options.text: Where passengers cannot stand.
Where passengers board and exit.
Part of the air conditioning system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where passengers cannot stand.
questions.explanation: On a bus with standing passengers, passengers cannot stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. A line or marking on the floor shows this area. This is called a standee line.

questions.question: Carry-on bags should be placed:

options.text: In front of the back door.
In front of the front door.
Where they do not block any emergency exits.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where they do not block any emergency exits.
questions.explanation: Do not place bags in doorways or aisles. All bags must be placed so passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will:

options.text: Change a tire.
Tell the examiner what you would check and why.
Estimate the weight of a trailer load.
Change a windshield wiper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you would check and why.
questions.explanation: On the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Buses should never carry:

options.text: Medical drugs.
Small arms ammunition.
Emergency hospital supplies.
Radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials.
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials where passengers sit. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and medications are allowed.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump straight from the seat to the ground.
Always touch the vehicle with at least one hand.
Face the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting during the vehicle control test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can result in automatic failure.

questions.question: In cold weather, bridges usually freeze:

options.text: After the rest of the road.
Before the rest of the road.
At the same time as the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the rest of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Be extra careful on bridges and overpasses when it is cold and wet.

questions.question: Before a bus enters a curve, the driver should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Buses should always enter curves slowly. Be extra careful when entering a curve on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: If you may be late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Drive faster.
Use flashing lights to make other drivers move.
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.
Get upset.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and accept any delays. Avoid dangerous or aggressive driving. When planning a trip, add extra time for possible delays.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab because of:

options.text: A broken exhaust system.
Using the wrong fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A broken exhaust system.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can let poisonous fumes enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Only happens at very high speeds.
Can happen at speeds as slow as 30 mph.
Happens most when tire pressure is too high.
Happens most when tires have good tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen at speeds as slow as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at 30 mph or slower if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or when tire tread is worn.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Probably knows what is happening around them.
May not know what is happening around them.
Can hear traffic sounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not know what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around joggers and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle coming and could do something dangerous because they don't know you are there.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Ability to focus
Daydreaming
Yawning often
Drifting out of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful because there is little you can do about things far away.
Good because it helps you spot hazards early.
Not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good because it helps you spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and respond safely.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Should not be used on any vehicle.
Should not be used on the front wheels of a bus.
Should not be used on trucks carrying gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: When going down a hill, you can use less braking by:

options.text: Shifting to a higher gear.
Shifting to a lower gear.
Shifting to neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, slow down and shift to a lower gear. This helps you control your vehicle without using too much brake. Heavy braking downhill can overheat the brakes and reduce their power.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge is too high, you should:

options.text: Keep driving.
Pull over and check what is wrong.
Turn on the air conditioner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature is too high, stop driving right away and find out why. There may be a problem that could cause engine failure or a fire.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: The trailer is straight.
There is no trailer.
The vehicle is slightly uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: On vehicles with trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly if the trailers are straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, you should:

options.text: Not back up in a straight line.
Not fix drift until you are far off course.
Pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing, pull forward to reposition your vehicle as needed. Fix any drift right away by turning the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
